items.stem: Write the floral formula of the family Solanaceae.
items.answer: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2) with a line below G (superior ovary), stamens epipetalous.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the correct formula.

items.stem: Give two differences between G1 phase and G0 (quiescent stage).
items.answer: G1 phase: cell grows continuously; between mitosis and the start of DNA replication. G0 (quiescent stage): metabolically active; cells exit G1.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. G1 phase – cell grows continuously; between mitosis and the start of DNA replication; G0 (quiescent stage) – metabolically active; cells exit G1.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as disorder due to hypersecretion or disorder due to hyposecretion: cretinism, Graves' disease (exophthalmic goitre), Addison's disease, dwarfism.
items.answer: cretinism – disorder due to hyposecretion; Graves' disease (exophthalmic goitre) – disorder due to hypersecretion; Addison's disease – disorder due to hyposecretion; dwarfism – disorder due to hyposecretion.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: cretinism – disorder due to hyposecretion; Graves' disease (exophthalmic goitre) – disorder due to hypersecretion; Addison's disease – disorder due to hyposecretion; dwarfism – disorder due to hyposecretion.

items.stem: A cell organelle has these features: major site for synthesis of lipids; no ribosomes on its surface. Identify the organelle. Give a reason.
items.answer: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the smooth endoplasmic reticulum; 1 mark: the features major site for synthesis of lipids; no ribosomes on its surface are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Give two differences between a virus and a lichen.
items.answer: A virus: genetic material is either RNA or DNA, never both; inert outside a host cell. A lichen: do not grow in polluted areas; association of an alga and a fungus.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. a virus – genetic material is either RNA or DNA, never both; inert outside a host cell; a lichen – do not grow in polluted areas; association of an alga and a fungus.

items.stem: Compare cardiac muscle and cartilage on any three points.
items.answer: Cardiac muscle: intercalated discs; present only in the heart; involuntary contraction. Cartilage: solid, pliable intercellular material; resists compression; cells (chondrocytes) enclosed in small cavities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. cardiac muscle – intercalated discs; present only in the heart; involuntary contraction; cartilage – solid, pliable intercellular material; resists compression; cells (chondrocytes) enclosed in small cavities.

items.stem: Distinguish between acoelomates, pseudocoelomates and coelomates with one example each.
items.answer: Acoelomates – no body cavity (Platyhelminthes, e.g. Taenia); pseudocoelomates – cavity not lined by mesoderm, mesoderm in scattered pouches (Aschelminthes, e.g. Ascaris); coelomates – cavity lined by mesoderm (annelids to chordates, e.g. earthworm).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Compare spring wood and sapwood on any three points.
items.answer: Spring wood: many xylary elements with wide vessels; lower density; formed when the cambium is very active. Sapwood: also called alburnum; conducts water and minerals; light coloured.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. spring wood – many xylary elements with wide vessels; lower density; formed when the cambium is very active; sapwood – also called alburnum; conducts water and minerals; light coloured.

items.stem: Why is identification and nomenclature necessary? Name the codes that give the rules for naming plants and animals.
items.answer: There are millions of organisms and local names vary from place to place, so a standard name known all over the world is needed; organisms are first identified correctly and then named. Plants – ICBN; animals – ICZN.
items.markingKey: 1 mark need; 1 mark ICBN; 1 mark ICZN.

items.stem: Explain the three layers of the glomerular filtration membrane.
items.answer: Endothelium of glomerular blood vessels; epithelium of Bowman's capsule (podocytes arranged with filtration slits or slit pores); and the basement membrane between them. Blood is filtered so finely that almost all plasma constituents except proteins pass.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each layer.

items.stem: Give three differences between inspiration and expiration.
items.answer: Inspiration: external intercostal muscles contract; intra-pulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric; diaphragm contracts and flattens. Expiration: diaphragm relaxes and returns to dome shape; intra-pulmonary pressure rises above atmospheric; thoracic and pulmonary volumes decrease.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. inspiration – external intercostal muscles contract; intra-pulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric; diaphragm contracts and flattens; expiration – diaphragm relaxes and returns to dome shape; intra-pulmonary pressure rises above atmospheric; thoracic and pulmonary volumes decrease.

items.stem: Distinguish between a nucleoside and a nucleotide with one example each.
items.answer: Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar, e.g. adenosine, guanosine, thymidine, uridine, cytidine. Nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate, e.g. adenylic acid, thymidylic acid, guanylic acid, uridylic acid, cytidylic acid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each definition; 1 mark examples.

items.stem:
Priya (Rh⁻) is expecting her second child; her first child was Rh⁺. Her doctor in Indore had given her an injection soon after the first delivery.
(i) What condition was the injection meant to prevent? (1 mark)
(ii) What did the injection contain? (1 mark)
(iii) Explain why the first child was not affected but the second could be. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Erythroblastosis foetalis. (ii) Anti-Rh antibodies. (iii) During the first pregnancy the bloods are separated by the placenta, but during delivery some foetal Rh⁺ blood enters the mother, who makes anti-Rh antibodies; in later pregnancies these cross the placenta and destroy the RBCs of an Rh⁺ foetus.

items.stem:
In an alga, the only diploid cell in the life cycle is the zygote, which divides by meiosis.
(i) Name this life cycle pattern. (1 mark)
(ii) Give one example. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the pattern differ in a moss? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Haplontic. (ii) Volvox / Spirogyra / Chlamydomonas. (iii) Moss is haplo-diplontic: the sporophyte is multicellular (foot, seta, capsule) though dependent on the gametophyte; meiosis occurs in the capsule to form spores.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a C4 plant and a C3 plant on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A plant shows these features: first stable product is OAA. Identify the type of plant – a C4 plant or a C3 plant? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A C4 plant: first stable product is OAA; primary CO₂ acceptor is PEP; Kranz anatomy present. A C3 plant: first stable product is PGA; primary CO₂ acceptor is RuBP; no Kranz anatomy. (b) A C4 plant.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a C4 plant; 1 mark: “first stable product is OAA” is a feature of a C4 plant.

items.stem: Describe the human axial skeleton. Classify joints with examples.
items.answer: 80 bones: skull (22 – 8 cranial, 14 facial), hyoid, 6 ear ossicles; vertebral column of 26 vertebrae – cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, sacral 1 (fused), coccygeal 1 (fused); sternum; 12 pairs of ribs – true (1–7), vertebrochondral/false (8–10), floating (11–12). Joints: fibrous (sutures of skull), cartilaginous (between vertebrae), synovial – ball and socket (humerus and pectoral girdle), hinge (knee), pivot (atlas and axis), gliding (carpals), saddle (carpal and metacarpal of thumb).
items.markingKey: 3 marks axial skeleton; 2 marks joints.

items.stem: Distinguish between arithmetic and geometric growth with equations and curves. What are the conditions for growth?
items.answer: Arithmetic: one daughter cell divides, the other differentiates; Lt = L₀ + rt; linear curve (root elongating at constant rate). Geometric: both divide; initial lag, exponential (log) phase, stationary phase – sigmoid curve; W₁ = W₀e^(rt). Conditions: water (turgidity, enzymatic activity), oxygen (metabolic energy), nutrients, optimum temperature, light and gravity.
items.markingKey: 3 marks growth types; 2 marks conditions.

options: synaptic vesicles move to and fuse with the plasma membrane → neurotransmitters released into the synaptic cleft → neurotransmitters bind to receptors on the post-synaptic membrane → ion channels open and a new potential develops

items.stem: Which of the following statements about photorespiration and factors affecting photosynthesis is incorrect?
items.answer: Water stress has no effect on photosynthesis.

items.stem: A region of the renal tubule is described: permeable to water; almost impermeable to electrolytes; filtrate becomes concentrated as it moves down. Identify the region. Give a reason.

items.stem: Give two differences between a monocot seed (maize) and a dicot seed (bean).
items.answer: A monocot seed (maize): seed coat membranous and fused with the fruit wall; bulky endosperm separated by an aleurone layer. A dicot seed (bean): two cotyledons, often fleshy with food; seed coat with testa and tegmen.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. a monocot seed (maize) – seed coat membranous and fused with the fruit wall; bulky endosperm separated by an aleurone layer; a dicot seed (bean) – two cotyledons, often fleshy with food; seed coat with testa and tegmen.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as pyrimidine or purine: guanine, uracil, adenine.
items.answer: guanine – purine; uracil – pyrimidine; adenine – purine.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: guanine – purine; uracil – pyrimidine; adenine – purine.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as disease caused by a viroid or disease caused by a virus: influenza, AIDS, herpes, potato spindle tuber disease.
items.answer: influenza – disease caused by a virus; AIDS – disease caused by a virus; herpes – disease caused by a virus; potato spindle tuber disease – disease caused by a viroid.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: influenza – disease caused by a virus; AIDS – disease caused by a virus; herpes – disease caused by a virus; potato spindle tuber disease – disease caused by a viroid.

items.stem: Give two differences between botanical garden and zoological park.
items.answer: Botanical garden: used for reference; each plant labelled with scientific name and family. Zoological park: wild animals kept in protected environments under human care; environments close to natural habitats.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. botanical garden – used for reference; each plant labelled with scientific name and family; zoological park – wild animals kept in protected environments under human care; environments close to natural habitats.

items.stem: Distinguish between the G1, S and G2 phases of interphase.
items.answer: G1 – cell metabolically active and grows, DNA not replicated; S – DNA replication, DNA doubles 2C → 4C, chromosome number unchanged; G2 – protein synthesis in preparation for mitosis, growth continues.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Name the three cranial meninges from outside to inside and give the protective structure surrounding them.
items.answer: Dura mater (outer), arachnoid (middle, very thin), pia mater (inner, in contact with brain tissue); the brain is protected by the skull (cranium).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each meninx in the correct order.

items.stem: Give three functions of mesosomes.
items.answer: Help in cell wall formation; DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells; respiration and secretion; increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three.

items.stem: Compare columnar epithelium and ciliated epithelium on any three points.
items.answer: Columnar epithelium: nuclei located at the base; single layer of tall, slender cells; lines the stomach and intestine. Ciliated epithelium: moves particles or mucus in a specific direction; lines bronchioles; lines fallopian tubes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. columnar epithelium – nuclei located at the base; single layer of tall, slender cells; lines the stomach and intestine; ciliated epithelium – moves particles or mucus in a specific direction; lines bronchioles; lines fallopian tubes.

items.stem: Compare the alveoli and the tissues on any three points.
items.answer: The alveoli: low pCO₂ (40 mm Hg); oxyhaemoglobin is formed; lesser H⁺ concentration and lower temperature. The tissues: low pO₂ (40 mm Hg); oxyhaemoglobin dissociates; high H⁺ concentration and higher temperature.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. the alveoli – low pCO₂ (40 mm Hg); oxyhaemoglobin is formed; lesser H⁺ concentration and lower temperature; the tissues – low pO₂ (40 mm Hg); oxyhaemoglobin dissociates; high H⁺ concentration and higher temperature.

items.stem: Name the three types of movement shown by human cells and give one example of each.
items.answer: Amoeboid – macrophages and leucocytes (pseudopodia, also involving microfilaments); ciliary – removal of dust by cilia in the trachea, passage of ova in the female tract; muscular – movement of limbs, jaws, tongue.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Distinguish between non-cyclic photophosphorylation and photolysis of water on any three points.
items.answer: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation: O₂ is released; both PS II and PS I involved; electrons from water reach NADP⁺. Photolysis of water: supplies electrons to replace those lost by PS II; associated with PS II; occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. non-cyclic photophosphorylation – O₂ is released; both PS II and PS I involved; electrons from water reach NADP⁺; photolysis of water – supplies electrons to replace those lost by PS II; associated with PS II; occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.

items.stem:

(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were a membrane-bound receptor? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) An intracellular receptor (ii) hormone enters the cell (iii) used by protein hormones like FSH; hormone does not enter the cell

(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were organ level? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Tissue level (ii) cells performing the same function arranged into tissues (iii) tissues grouped to form organs; each organ specialised for a function
items.markingKey: (i) tissue level – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: cells performing the same function arranged into tissues – 1 mark. (iii) for organ level: tissues grouped to form organs; each organ specialised for a function; seen in platyhelminthes – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between mosses and liverworts on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A plant shows these features: elaborate spore dispersal mechanism. Identify the group – mosses or liverworts? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Mosses: first stage is a filamentous protonema; leafy stage with an upright stem and spirally arranged leaves; well-developed sporophyte with foot, seta and capsule. Liverworts: thalloid plant body that is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substratum; asexual reproduction by gemmae in gemma cups; sporophyte differentiated into foot, seta and capsule. (b) Mosses.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: mosses; 1 mark: “elaborate spore dispersal mechanism” is a feature of mosses.

items.stem: What is seed dormancy? Give its causes and the methods of overcoming it. Briefly explain photoperiodism.
items.answer: Dormancy – failure to germinate under favourable external conditions due to internal factors. Causes: hard impermeable seed coat, chemical inhibitors (ABA, phenolics, para-ascorbic acid), immature embryo. Overcoming: scarification, gibberellic acid, nitrates, changing light and temperature. Photoperiodism – response to day/night duration; long day, short day and day-neutral plants; leaves perceive the stimulus; hormonal signal to shoot apex.
items.markingKey: 3 marks dormancy; 2 marks photoperiodism.

items.stem: What are the assumptions of the respiratory balance sheet? Explain why the respiratory pathway is considered amphibolic.
items.answer: Assumptions: sequential, orderly pathway (glycolysis → TCA → ETS); NADH from glycolysis enters mitochondria for oxidative phosphorylation; no intermediate used to synthesise other compounds; only glucose respired, no alternative substrates enter. Net 38 ATP theoretical. Amphibolic: fats enter as acetyl CoA/PGAL and acetyl CoA is withdrawn for fatty acid synthesis; proteins enter after deamination and intermediates are withdrawn for amino acid synthesis; so both catabolism and anabolism.
items.markingKey: 2 marks assumptions; 3 marks amphibolic.

items.stem: Which term describes a peptide hormone secreted by the atrial wall of the heart that decreases blood pressure?
items.answer: atrial natriuretic factor (ANF)
items.markingKey: (d) Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF): a peptide hormone secreted by the atrial wall of the heart that decreases blood pressure.
options: cholecystokinin (CCK)
secretin
gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP)
atrial natriuretic factor (ANF)

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events in sexual reproduction of fungi?
items.answer: plasmogamy → karyogamy → meiosis in the zygote

karyogamy → plasmogamy → meiosis in the zygote

items.stem: How many molecules of NADPH are needed to synthesise 4 molecules of glucose (24 CO₂ fixed) in a C3 plant?
items.markingKey: (d) Per CO₂: 3 ATP and 2 NADPH in the Calvin cycle (C4 plants use 2 extra ATP per CO₂). For 24 CO₂: NADPH = 48.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about algae is incorrect?
items.answer: Most brown algae are found in fresh water.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of glycolysis?
items.answer: glucose → fructose-6-phosphate → 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate → phosphoenol pyruvate

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the basis of classification of animals is correct?
items.answer: Coelenterates have tissue level of organisation.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about respiratory organs and the human respiratory system is incorrect?
items.answer: Gas exchange occurs in the trachea and bronchi.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as chromosome with the centromere slightly away from the middle or chromosome with the centromere in the middle: sub-metacentric, metacentric.
items.answer: sub-metacentric – chromosome with the centromere slightly away from the middle; metacentric – chromosome with the centromere in the middle.

items.stem: Give two differences between squamous epithelium and areolar tissue.
items.answer: Squamous epithelium: single thin layer of flattened cells; irregular cell boundaries. Areolar tissue: serves as a support framework for epithelium; loose arrangement of cells and fibres.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. squamous epithelium – single thin layer of flattened cells; irregular cell boundaries; areolar tissue – serves as a support framework for epithelium; loose arrangement of cells and fibres.

items.stem: Give two differences between gout and osteoporosis.
items.answer: Gout: a joint disorder; accumulation of uric acid crystals. Osteoporosis: decreased bone mass; age-related disorder.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. gout – a joint disorder; accumulation of uric acid crystals; osteoporosis – decreased bone mass; age-related disorder.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as steroid hormone or amino-acid derivative hormone: noradrenaline, adrenaline, progesterone, cortisol.
items.answer: noradrenaline – amino-acid derivative hormone; adrenaline – amino-acid derivative hormone; progesterone – steroid hormone; cortisol – steroid hormone.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: noradrenaline – amino-acid derivative hormone; adrenaline – amino-acid derivative hormone; progesterone – steroid hormone; cortisol – steroid hormone.

items.stem: Give two differences between basal placentation and marginal placentation.
items.answer: Basal placentation: e.g. sunflower; placenta develops at the base of the ovary. Marginal placentation: ovules borne on the ridge in two rows; ovary one-chambered.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. basal placentation – e.g. sunflower; placenta develops at the base of the ovary; marginal placentation – ovules borne on the ridge in two rows; ovary one-chambered.

items.stem: Write three economic or ecological uses of bacteria mentioned in NCERT.
items.answer: Methanogens produce biogas; bacteria make curd from milk and produce antibiotics; nitrogen-fixing bacteria and cyanobacteria fix nitrogen; chemosynthetic bacteria recycle N, P, Fe and S.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three.

items.stem: Give three causes of seed dormancy and one method to overcome each.
items.answer: Hard impermeable seed coat – scarification (mechanical abrasion, shaking); chemical inhibitors such as ABA, phenolics, para-ascorbic acid – gibberellic acid or nitrates; immature embryo – changing light and temperature conditions/after-ripening.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Why is photorespiration considered a wasteful process? Why does it not occur in C4 plants?
items.answer: RuBisCO combines RuBP with O₂ forming PGA and phosphoglycolate; there is no synthesis of sugar or ATP, CO₂ is released and ATP is consumed. In C4 plants malate releases CO₂ in bundle sheath cells, raising its concentration so RuBisCO acts as a carboxylase.
items.markingKey: 2 marks wasteful; 1 mark C4.

items.stem: Compare a dicot and a monocot on any three points.
items.answer: A dicot: flowers usually tetramerous or pentamerous; two cotyledons in the seed; reticulate venation in leaves. A monocot: fibrous root system; parallel venation in leaves; one cotyledon in the seed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. a dicot – flowers usually tetramerous or pentamerous; two cotyledons in the seed; reticulate venation in leaves; a monocot – fibrous root system; parallel venation in leaves; one cotyledon in the seed.

items.stem: Give one example each of the following secondary metabolites: (i) alkaloid, (ii) toxin, (iii) drug.
items.answer: (i) Morphine or codeine; (ii) abrin or ricin; (iii) vinblastin or curcumin.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: How do fats and proteins enter the respiratory pathway?
items.answer: Fats → glycerol and fatty acids; fatty acids are degraded to acetyl CoA and enter the Krebs cycle; glycerol converted to PGAL enters glycolysis. Proteins → amino acids by proteases; after deamination, depending on structure, they enter as pyruvic acid, acetyl CoA or within the Krebs cycle.
items.markingKey: 1½ marks each.

items.stem: Give three characteristic features of class Aves.
items.answer: Feathers; beak; forelimbs modified into wings; pneumatic bones; crop and gizzard; four-chambered heart; homoiothermous; oviparous.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three.

items.stem:
A mountaineer climbing in Ladakh breathes faster at high altitude. His doctor explains that his blood still carries most oxygen bound to a pigment in RBCs.
(i) Name the pigment and the compound it forms with O₂. (1 mark)
(ii) What percentage of O₂ is carried this way? (1 mark)
(iii) Name the centre that regulates breathing rhythm and the chemical factors that normally stimulate it. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Haemoglobin; oxyhaemoglobin. (ii) About 97%. (iii) Respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla; increase in CO₂ and H⁺ ions sensed by the chemosensitive area (and receptors in aortic arch and carotid artery).

items.stem:
A part of the human nephron or kidney has these features: site of ultrafiltration; tuft of capillaries; formed by the afferent arteriole.
(i) Identify the part. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the proximal convoluted tubule? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The glomerulus (ii) blood leaves by the efferent arteriole (iii) in the cortex; major site of reabsorption
items.markingKey: (i) the glomerulus – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: blood leaves by the efferent arteriole – 1 mark. (iii) for the proximal convoluted tubule: lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium; highly coiled; in the cortex – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Describe the structure of a neuron with a labelled diagram. Classify neurons with examples.
items.answer: Cell body with cytoplasm, organelles and Nissl's granules; dendrites – short branched fibres with Nissl's granules, carry impulses towards the cell body; axon – long fibre, distal end branched, terminating in synaptic knobs with vesicles of neurotransmitters, carries impulses away. Myelinated (Schwann cells, myelin sheath, nodes of Ranvier – spinal and cranial nerves) and unmyelinated. Multipolar (cerebral cortex), bipolar (retina), unipolar (embryonic).
items.markingKey: 3 marks structure; 2 marks classification.

items.stem: Describe the phases of the cell cycle. What is G0 phase? Why is interphase not called a resting phase?
items.answer: Interphase – G1 (growth, metabolic activity, no DNA replication), S (DNA replication 2C → 4C, chromosome number unchanged; centriole duplication in animals), G2 (protein synthesis, growth); M phase – karyokinesis and cytokinesis. G0 – quiescent, metabolically active, non-dividing cells (e.g. heart cells), replace lost cells when needed. Interphase is the period of preparation for division with growth and DNA replication.
items.markingKey: 3 marks phases; 1 mark G0; 1 mark interphase.

items.stem: Describe the three tissue systems of a plant and the components of each.
items.answer: Epidermal tissue system – epidermis, cuticle, stomata (guard cells, subsidiary cells), trichomes and root hairs. Ground tissue system – all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles: parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma; cortex, pericycle, pith, medullary rays; mesophyll in leaves. Vascular tissue system – xylem and phloem; bundles radial (roots), conjoint collateral; open (dicot stem, with cambium) or closed (monocot).
items.markingKey: 2 marks epidermal; 1½ ground; 1½ vascular.
